hip-thrust.description: A bench-supported hip extension that develops the glutes through a strong horizontal drive.
instructions: Sit with your upper back against a bench, feet flat, and the padded bar centered across your hip crease.
Brace your trunk and drive through your feet as your upper back pivots on the bench and your hips rise.
Finish with hips extended and shins nearly vertical, then lower your hips smoothly toward the floor.
Keep your knees tracking over your toes and avoid arching your lower back at the top.

smith-machine-hip-thrust.description: A fixed-bar hip thrust that trains powerful glute extension along a guided path.
instructions: Place a bench behind the Smith bar, rest your upper back on it, and position the padded bar across your hip crease.
Set your feet flat, release the hooks, and drive the bar upward by extending your hips without pushing the bench backward.
Squeeze your glutes when your torso is level, then lower the bar under control and re-rack it when finished.
Keep your ribs down, chin tucked, and knees aligned with your feet throughout the guided path.

glute-bridge.description: A floor-based hip extension that isolates the glutes with a stable bodyweight position.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat near your hips, and arms resting beside you.
Brace your midsection and press through your feet to lift your pelvis while your shoulders stay grounded.
Squeeze your glutes when shoulders, hips, and knees form a line, then lower until your hips touch down softly.
Keep your knees from collapsing inward and do not finish by overextending your lower back.

cable-pull-through.description: A cable-resisted hip hinge that keeps tension on the glutes as the hips move backward and forward.
instructions: Face away from a low pulley, straddle the rope attachment, and step forward with the rope held between your legs.
Soften your knees and push your hips back while the cable travels between your thighs and your spine stays neutral.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall, squeeze your glutes, and reverse the hinge under control.
Let your arms act as straps and avoid turning the finish into a backward lean.

cable-glute-kickback.description: A standing cable hip extension that targets one glute at a time with continuous resistance.
instructions: Attach an ankle cuff to a low pulley, face the stack, and hold the frame while standing firmly on the free leg.
With a soft working knee, sweep the cuffed leg backward in a controlled arc without swinging your torso.
Stop when the glute is fully shortened, then guide the leg forward until it returns beneath your hip.
Keep both hip bones facing the stack and avoid using your lower back to gain extra range.

machine-glute-kickback.description: A supported single-leg hip extension that directs the machine's resistance into the glutes.
instructions: Settle your torso against the support, grip the handles, and place one foot securely on the working plate.
Brace against the pad and press the plate backward by extending your hip at a steady pace.
Finish with a firm glute squeeze before allowing the plate to return smoothly to the start.
Keep your pelvis square to the machine and do not twist or arch to move the plate farther.

hip-abduction-machine.description: A seated outward hip movement that trains the abductors and side glutes against machine resistance.
instructions: Sit with your back supported, feet on the rests, and the outside of each thigh against its pad.
Press your knees apart in a smooth arc while keeping your hips centered on the seat.
Pause at your controlled outer range, then let the pads return inward without touching abruptly.
Keep your torso still and resist bouncing or forcing your knees beyond a comfortable path.

cable-hip-abduction.description: A standing single-leg abduction that challenges the outer hip against a low cable's pull.
instructions: Stand side-on to a low pulley with the cuff on the ankle farthest from the stack and hold the frame for balance.
Keep the working leg long and sweep it sideways away from the pulley without shifting your trunk.
Pause before your pelvis tilts, then guide the leg back across the cable's pull to the start.
Point your hips forward and keep the stance knee soft so the outer hip drives the motion.

hip-adduction-machine.description: A seated inward hip movement that isolates the inner thighs through a controlled machine arc.
instructions: Sit upright with your back supported, feet on the rests, and the inside of each thigh against its pad.
Draw your knees toward each other smoothly while keeping your hips and back in contact with the seat.
Pause as the pads come together, then reopen your legs slowly to the starting position.
Keep both sides moving evenly and avoid bouncing out of the open position.

cable-hip-adduction.description: A standing cable adduction that trains one inner thigh as the leg crosses toward the midline.
instructions: Stand side-on to a low pulley, cuff the ankle nearest the stack, and hold a stable support with the opposite hand.
Keep the cuffed leg long and sweep it inward across the front of your stance leg without rotating your hips.
Pause at the inward finish, then guide the leg back toward the pulley under steady control.
Stay tall over the stance foot and keep its knee soft rather than leaning away from the cable.

standing-calf-raise.description: A straight-leg machine raise that trains the calves through controlled ankle extension.
instructions: Place your shoulders under the pads and the balls of your feet on the platform with your heels free to move.
Stand tall with softly extended knees and press through your forefeet to raise your heels smoothly.
Pause high on your toes, then lower your heels under control through the available platform range.
Keep your ankles tracking over your feet and avoid bouncing from the bottom position.

seated-calf-raise.description: A bent-knee calf raise that emphasizes the lower calf while the thighs remain secured.
instructions: Sit with the balls of your feet on the platform, heels free, and the thigh pad secured just above your knees.
Press through your forefeet to lift your heels while your knees remain fixed beneath the pad.
Hold the top briefly, then lower your heels slowly before beginning the next raise.
Keep your feet aligned with your knees and avoid rocking your torso to move the lever.

smith-machine-calf-raise.description: A guided standing calf raise that allows focused ankle movement beneath a fixed bar path.
instructions: Set the Smith bar across your upper back, stand with feet hip-width, and balance the bar over your midfoot.
Unrack the bar, keep your legs long with soft knees, and rise onto your toes in a smooth vertical path.
Pause at full ankle extension, then lower your heels gently to the floor and re-rack after the set.
Keep your ankles upright and avoid bouncing or leaning into the guided bar.

dumbbell-calf-raise.description: A free-weight standing raise that strengthens the calves while demanding steady balance.
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width, a dumbbell at each side, and your weight balanced across both forefeet.
Press through the balls of your feet to raise both heels together without bending your knees for momentum.
Pause on your toes, then lower both heels gently to the floor before repeating.
Keep your ankles upright and your torso stacked rather than swaying the dumbbells.

single-leg-calf-raise.description: A unilateral bodyweight raise that builds calf strength and ankle control on each side.
instructions: Stand on one foot beside a stable support, lift the other foot clear, and balance over the working forefoot.
Press through the ball of the standing foot to raise your heel while keeping the working leg steady.
Pause at the top, then lower the heel slowly to the starting level before the next repetition.
Keep the ankle from rolling inward or outward and use the support only to maintain balance.

leg-press-calf-raise.description: A leg-press variation that isolates ankle extension while the torso and hips stay supported.
instructions: Sit securely in the leg press and place the balls of both feet on the lower edge of the sled with heels free.
Keep your knees softly extended and press the sled away by pointing your ankles without moving your hips.
Pause with your heels raised, then let them travel back under control as your ankles flex.
Maintain full forefoot contact with the platform and do not lock or bend your knees during the raise.
